sentences.text: Second respondent approached the District Court, Haveri with a request for grant of anticipatory bail by expressing real apprehension of his arrest in respect of an intended compla int by the petitioner herein.

4. Learned District Judge, Haveri entertained the bail application and following the NC:
2023:KHC-D:7559 dictum of the H on'ble Apex Court in the case of Gurubaksh Singh Sibbia et c. Vs.
The Stat e of Punjab reported in AIR 1980 SCC 1632 granted anticipatory bail initially for a period of three months and the same was extended.
5.

sentences.text:
The grouse of t he petit ioner is that since the anticipatory bail is obtained by the petitioner even before lodging of the complaint, the conditions that are imposed by learned District Judge shall not impose any condit ion where the petitioner is required to join the investigation and co-operate with the investigation process and therefore, he sought for cance llation of the bail.
6.

Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader and Shri. N. R. Kuppelur, submit that second respondent is ready to abide any other condit ion/s that would be imposed by NC:
2023:KHC-D:7559 this Court and no case is made out for cancellation of the bail and sought for dismissal of the pet ition.

7. Having heard the parties in detail about the facts of the case, this Court is of the considered opinion that learned District Judge has rightly exercised the discretionary and special power vested in her under Sect ion 438 of Cr.P.C. and has rightly granted the anticipatory bail initially for a period of three months as real apprehension of arrest made out by second respondent herein.
8.
However, after the said bail order came to be passed, a complaint came to be filed by the petitioner herein and it is being invest igated by the concerned police.

While granting the anticipatory bail, learned Distr ict Judge has imposed the following conditions:
"1. The petitioner shall not tamper with the applicant directly or ind irectly.
2. He shall not threate n the applicant a nd also maintain peace and tranquility in the locality of the applicant.
3. He shall not be involved in any criminal activities.
4. This order will be in force for a period of 3 mo nths from the d ate of this order."

10. As could be seen from the conditions imposed by learned District Judge, there is no specif ic condition imposed by learned District Judge to direct second respondent to join the investigation and co-operate with the case in the event of filing a case.

sentences.text:
Since the offence alleged against second respondent herein is under Sect ion 376 of Cr.P.C., NC:
2023:KHC-D:7559 the samples are required to be collected and so also potency test is to be conducted insofar as second respondent is concerned.
12. Therefore, second respondent is required to join the invest igat ion and co-operate with the investigation.

13. Accordingly, apart from the condit ions imposed by learned District Judge in the order dated 04.02.2023 which has been made absolute, this Court is of the considered opinion that direct ing second respondent to join the investigation if not already joined and c o-operate with the investigation agency in providing the samples etc., would meet the ends of justice and would also quell all apprehensions of the petitioner as well.

14. Accordingly, t he following order is passed:
NC: 2023:KHC-D:7559 ORDER Petition st and disposed of by direct ing second respondent to joined the investigation if not already join and co- operate with the investigation agency.

I n that regard, petitioner shall mark his attendance before the investigation officer on 31.07.2023 at 10.00 a.m. The investigation officer is at liberty to collect the samples if any and also take the petitioner for medical examination/potency test.

Sd/-
